info.title: OpenAsy Uptime API
info.summary: Checks, their state and outages, and a public status page. Runners run the checks; the server never probes anything.
info.description:
Every screen of Uptime uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Checks are defined here and run by a runner: the script at `/uptime-runner.mjs`, started from a CI cron or any machine, with `UPTIME_INGEST_TOKEN`. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003). `/status` and `/api/v1/status/public` need no sign-in and show only checks marked public.

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

get.description:
What the public status page at `/status` shows, as data.

Needs no sign-in.

For a runner, such as the script at `/uptime-runner.mjs`. It holds targets, so it needs the runner token.

Takes UPTIME_INGEST_TOKEN, or an API token with the editor role.

200.description: Every check that is not paused, with its target.

post.description:
What a runner saw, up to 500 at a time (gzip is fine). The whole batch is refused if one result is wrong. A result older than the newest one of its check is kept but does not move its state.

Takes UPTIME_INGEST_TOKEN, or an API token with the editor role.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only checks in this state, as shown (stale is unknown).

201.description: Created. Nothing runs it until a runner does.

delete.description:
Deletes its results and outages.

Needs the admin role.

200.description: Paused: runners skip it, it is never stale, and the status page shows maintenance.
Newest first, within the retention period.
From OPENASY_PRODUCTS, for the product switcher.

get.description: Plain HTML with no script, for anyone. It shows the same as `/api/v1/status/public`.
A script with no dependencies that runs on Node 20 or later: fetch it, set UPTIME_URL and UPTIME_INGEST_TOKEN, and run it from a CI cron.

200.description: Metrics in the Prometheus text format.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when uptime runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the uptime origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_uptime_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when uptime is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

ingestToken.description: `UPTIME_INGEST_TOKEN`: for runners. It can fetch the checks and send results, nothing else.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

Expect.description: What counts as a pass. `http`: `status` (default: any status below 400) and `text` the page must contain. `dns`: `recordType` (A, AAAA, CNAME or TXT; default A) and `record` that must be among the answers. `tls`: `minDays` the certificate must have left (default 14). `tcp` takes nothing.

State.description: `degraded`: failing, but fewer times in a row than `failuresToDown`. `unknown`: no result yet, or none for three intervals (`stale`).

intervalSeconds.description: How often a runner is expected to run it. A check is stale after three intervals without a result.

failuresToDown.description: Failures in a row before the check is down.

source.description: file: from the endpoints file (OPENASY_ENDPOINTS); changed there, so PATCH and DELETE answer 409. Pause and resume still work.

server.description: The server the endpoint runs on, by its name in the hosts file. Set from the endpoints file only.

uptime.description: Percent of the time the check was not in an outage, from its first result. Null until it has history.

latency.description: Milliseconds over the last 24 hours of passing results; only in a single check.

nextCursor.description: Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.

target.description: `http`: a web address. `tcp`: host:port. `dns`: a host name. `tls`: a host name, with :port if not 443.

public.description: Shown on the public status page by name, group and state.

target.description: `http`: a web address. `tcp`: host:port. `dns`: a host name. `tls`: a host name, with :port if not 443.

public.description: Shown on the public status page by name, group and state.

time.description: When the runner ran it; within the last day and not more than five minutes ahead. Default: now.

location.description: Where the runner ran, such as `github`.

nextCursor.description: Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.

startedAt.description: The first failure of the streak that took the check down.

nextCursor.description: Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.

endpointsFile.description: null when OPENASY_ENDPOINTS is not set.

PublicStatus.description: Only what an admin made public. No addresses, expectations, tags, details or ids.

EndpointsFile.description: The endpoints file (ADR 0052). It is read again within a minute of a change; a file that cannot be applied leaves the checks from its last good version.

appliedAt.description: When it was last read and applied; null if it never was.

error.description: Why the file on disk is not applied.

warnings.description: What to fix that did not stop the file from being applied.
